1840.s: Will you not raise those jealous veils which, I am certain, cover two angelic faces ?
1840.au: Maid Marian, the forest queen; | being a companion to "Robin Hood", | $c: by J.H. Stocqueler [pseud.] ...

1850.s: Fair as a Moorish maiden might be, the features which a jealous but transparent veil permitted to be seen were symmetrical and expressive, and were still surpassed by the grace of her light elastic form.
1850.au: Home and the world. | $c: By the author of "Souvenirs of a residence in Europe."

1860.s: Meredith had no difficulty in recognising the fragile figure of Maysunah, in spite of the jealous veil, which partially covered her form, and, conformably with Turkish custom, wholly hid her face.
1860.au: El Fureidîs. | $c: By the author of "The lamplighter" and "Mabel Vaughan."

1870.s: …tablets the graceful contour of the slight figure, as it bent lightly to her oars, every fold of her white dress, the long floating ribbons of pale blue, that she had flung backward over her shoulder, the jealous straw hat that hid the dear face from him, granting him but a glimpse of her clear cut profile, as she turned her eyes now to this bank, now to the other, to “keep her bearings.”
1870.au: Heavy yokes. | $c: By Janet H. Hadermann, [pseud.] ...

1880.s: "Call for me with the carriage at D 's drug store," she had said; so to D 's she hurried now when the sudden rain fell, gathering her handsome dress regretfully about her, jealous of the myriad drops that were defacing its freshness.
1880.au: No gentlemen, | $c: by Clara Louise Burnham.

1880.s: She is indeed just peeping over the jealous fur that so cruelly conceals the laughing lips, but the brilliant, mirthful eyes make up, almost, for that loss.
1880.au: A life's remorse, | $c: by the author of "Phyllis," "Molly Bawn," "Undercurrents," etc.

1880.s: …dismissing her attendants, and desiring them to leave her alone with the queen until the last moment of departure, hastened to disguise Berengaria in her own simple habit; in its flowing draperies, beneath the jealous folds of the long, ample veil, with the white virginal band which effectually repressed every truant wave of the queen's dark tresses, the disguise was complete — impenetrable.
1880.au: Matilda, princess of England. | A romance of the crusades, | $c: by Mme. Sophie Cottin ... From the French by Jennie W. Raum. Ed. by George E. Raum ...

1880.s: The prince gazed upon her beauty with increasing passion — content at first to gaze unrepelled; then, drawn as by invisible spells, he approached nearer; he dared not touch so much as a fold of her jealous veil, yet his heart beat violently and fire coursed through his burning veins.
1880.au: Matilda, princess of England. | A romance of the crusades, | $c: by Mme. Sophie Cottin ... From the French by Jennie W. Raum. Ed. by George E. Raum ...

1880.s: A jealous gown hides from the hungry glances the beautiful hips and white shoulders, but lets one imagine, under its folds, the form which is divine!
1880.au: Military life in Italy. | $c: Sketches by Edmondo de Amicis ... Tr. by Wilhelmina W. Cady ...

1890.s: She is indeed just peeping over the jealous fur that so cruelly conceals the laughing lips, but the brilliant, mirthful eyes make up, almost, for that loss.
1890.au: A life's remorse. | A novel. | $c: By the author of "Molly Bawn."

1890.s: May I not lift this jealous mask that hides your features from me?"
1890.au: Honoré de Balzac, | now for the first time completely translated into English...

1890.s: She had small white hands with round, tapering, pink tipped fingers, at this time covered by the jealous gloves; dainty feet that hardly seemed in keeping with her tall, graceful body; and as though Fortune had not cared to stint meet coverings for such a glorious figure, Ernai had all the money, and therefore all of the clothes…

…a formidable rival might be found in the married but not unmarriageable young woman of twenty-one, whose blue eyes and yellow ringlets shone with a brighter lustre from under the shade of the largest and most matronly cap attainable, and whose shrinking modesty might be a clever trick to allure men who were surfeited with the contrary.
1890.au: The veil of liberty, | a tale of the Girondins, | $c: by Péronne.

1890.s: He tried to distinguish the lady's face, and was singularly disappointed; a jealous veil hid her features, he could scarcely see her eyes gleaming behind the gauze, like two agates lit up by the sun.
1890.au: Comédie humaine,/ | $c: Edited by George Saintsbury (translated by Clara Bell, Ellen Marriage, James Waring and R.S. Scott).

1900.s: He tried to distinguish the lady’s face, and was singularly disappointed; a jealous veil hid her _ features, he could scarcely see her eyes gleaming behind the gauze, like two agates lit up by the sun.
1900.au: The Chouans : | A passion in the dessert / | $c: by Honoré de Balzac ; translated by Ellen Marriage with an introduction by George Saintsbury.

1900.s: And the others treated him as a lackey, overwhelmed him with scorn, jeered at his ragged coat, of which, at heart, they were jealous.
1900.au: Truth (Vérité), | $c: by Émile Zola; tr. by Ernest A. Vizetelly.

1900.s: Miss Bagsby's jacket was made for the meagre thinness of spare spinsterhood; the lovely lines of the young girl’s figure filled it, swelled it as an opening bud a jealous, too narrow sheath.
1900.au: Bagsby's daughter / | $c: by Bessie & Marie van Vorst ...

1900.s: This was evidently to be a dog day with me, and I speculated — picking the hairs of the large train dog from off my skirt that the puppies might not be jealous — just what this would signify in a dream book.
1900.au: The actress; | a novel, | $c: by Louise Closser Hale.

1910.s: The tipsy captain nodded him a welcome as he swaggered downstairs, stock, and coat, and waistcoat in hand, to his worship's toilette in the back kitchen.
1910.au: Lovel the widower, and other stories & sketches. | $c: With illus. by the author, George Cruikshank, Kenny Meadows, and Harry Furniss.

1910.s: But there were young, pretty ones, too, who often strolled by, looking sideways from the shelter of jealous sunbonnets.
1910.au: The emigrant trail, | $c: by Geraldine Bonner.

1910.s: Natalie gazed unswervingly at the sea and Paul gazed just as unswervingly at as much of her face as was visible to him under the edge of the jealous hat.
1910.au: The golden heart, | $c: by Ralph Henry Barbour ... with illustrations in color by Clarence F. Underwood and decorations by Edward Stratton Holloway.

1910.s: Even the little foot and slender ankle, freed by relaxation from the jealous skirt, helped to emphasise differences wide as those between a hummingbird and a pouter pigeon.
1910.au: The mystery of the barranca, | $c: by Herman Whitaker ...

1910.s: I saw her come down the grand staircase on the right, her white dress standing out against the red cloak, with a handkerchief over her head and fastened under her chin; the jealous lace fell a little over her eyes, but what did that matter?
1910.au: The lady with the camellias (Camille) / | $c: by Alexandre Dumas.
